obligations.note: The new route `POST /payees/{id}/reopen` maps to `manage_payees`, which is privileged in the access policy, yet it is declared with `mfa=False`. The exhaustive control test `test_privileged_routes_require_mfa` fails on exactly this route, and no valid exception covers it.
EXC-0203 was requested and 'approved' by sofia.santos, the change author. She holds no `risk_owner` role and is the requester, so the exception is invalid and cannot excuse the MFA-1 deviation.

The CI run on head `42d355f` has result `failure`: 1 of 172 tests failed, the registered MFA-1 control test. The JUnit report also does not match `run.json`: it is timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time, and came from host `dev-laptop-7.local` rather than `ci-runner-01`.
Ledger entry ACR-0404 (MFA-1, covering `routes.py`) lapses because `routes.py` changed in behaviour. The replacement evidence of the same strength, the exhaustive routes control test, fails.
Ticket CHG-25340 is a standard ticket approved by change manager grace.kim on 2026-10-15, before review. Its components (`payments.http`, `routes`, `service`, `store`) cover all four touched files.
mara.costa, a payments `change_approver` and not the author, gave a `code_review` approval on the head commit.
Both approvals name the single, head commit `42d355f`; there are no later commits.
The change touches security-sensitive components (`payments.routes`, `payments.http`, `payments.store`). ines.halvorsen, a `security_reviewer`, approved the head commit.

`store.py` changed, though the new `reopen_payee` writes no NPI columns. The only exhaustive evidence is a passing control test in a JUnit report whose provenance is inconsistent with the CI run, so it cannot be relied on.

The new statement is a fixed literal with `id` bound as a parameter, which looks compliant. The exhaustive SQL control-test pass, however, comes from a JUnit report with inconsistent provenance (timestamp after review time, different host).

The new `reopen_payee` records an audit event with actor, action, target and time via `_audit`. The only registered control test is sample coverage against an exhaustive requirement, and the CI evidence's provenance is doubtful.

`app.py` and `service.py` contain log call sites; the diff adds none, and the new path logs nothing. Only a sample control test exists, against an exhaustive requirement, and its CI report's provenance is doubtful.

summary: PR-1462 adds a privileged `manage_payees` route (`POST /payees/{id}/reopen`) without MFA, which violates MFA-1; the exhaustive routes control test fails on head. The change relies on exception EXC-0203, but the author approved it herself and she holds no `risk_owner` role, so EXC-1 is not met. CI on the final commit failed, and its JUnit report has inconsistent provenance. The prior MFA-1 evidence has lapsed with no passing replacement. Ticket, independent code review and security review are in order, but the change must be rejected.
